audit.label: unsupported
audit.why: Passage: ridge regression fixes the trouble multicollinearity causes; nothing is required.
audit.evidence: Ridge regression was developed as a possible solution to the imprecision of least square estimators when linear regression models have some multicollinear (highly correlated) independent variables—by creating a ridge regression estimator (RR).

audit.label: correct
audit.why: The lasso assumes sparse coefficients.
audit.evidence: The lasso method assumes that the coefficients of the linear model are sparse, meaning that few of them are non-zero.

audit.graph_says: oracle inequalities requires restricted eigenvalue condition
audit.label: correct
audit.why: The sharp oracle inequality is proved under the restricted eigenvalue condition.
audit.evidence: Koltchinskii, Lounici and Tsybakov proved a sharp oracle inequality for the fixed-design lasso under a restricted eigenvalue condition.

audit.label: correct
audit.why: Solving the lasso uses convex analysis.
audit.evidence: == Computing lasso solutions == [formula] The loss function of the lasso is not differentiable, but a wide variety of techniques from convex analysis and optimization theory have been developed to compute the solutions path of the lasso.

audit.label: correct
audit.why: Solving the lasso uses optimization theory.
audit.evidence: == Computing lasso solutions == [formula] The loss function of the lasso is not differentiable, but a wide variety of techniques from convex analysis and optimization theory have been developed to compute the solutions path of the lasso.
